newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's CIB bond offer oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's CIB bond offer oversubscribed.

text.p: A 300 million pound ($88.4 million) bond offer by Commercial International Bank of Egypt (CIB) closed last week after it was oversubscribed by 174 million pounds, a bank official said on Sunday.
The official, who declined to be named, told Reuters the offer closed on May 15 after it was opened for the minimum 10 days required.
The five-year, floating rate notes are in units of 1,000 pounds and pay every six months. The rate is fixed to the average annual return on 182-day t-bills plus 0.125 percent.

CIB is Egypt's largest private-sector bank and the only one with shares traded internationally. Its shareholders have said it could raise up to 900 million pounds by issuing pound or foreign currency bonds or floating-rate notes over two years.
